scenes.tts: A person has had their thyroid removed. They take only thyroxine, called T four. Yet their blood still holds the more active hormone, T three. Where does it come from? If the gland were the only source, there should be none.

scenes.tts: The thyroid secretes mostly T four. T four binds the thyroid hormone receptor much more weakly than T three does. So T four is best treated as a prohormone. Inside cells, T three binds receptors that regulate transcription. That is the form that acts.

scenes.tts: Tissues contain three enzymes called deiodinases. Each removes one iodine. D one and D two remove an iodine from the outer ring of T four. That makes T three, and it switches the hormone on. D three removes an iodine from the inner ring instead. That turns T four into reverse T three, which is inactive. The ring that loses the iodine decides: on or off.

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy, Braverman, Ingbar and Sterling tested this. They studied thirteen patients treated with T four. All but two were athyreotic, meaning without a functioning thyroid, or hypothyroid. They gave labelled T four, and separated the iodine compounds of serum by chromatography. Labelled T three appeared. A specially purified lot of tracer held less than zero point one percent T three, and gave the same result. In two more patients, T four went into a vein, bypassing the gut. Labelled T three still appeared.

scenes.tts: The result ruled in conversion outside the thyroid, in humans. The study did not identify the enzyme or the organ. It did not measure how much T three is made this way. Later work is commonly summarized as roughly eighty percent, in healthy people with enough iodine. That is an approximate estimate.

scenes.tts: Hormone does not simply diffuse into cells. It enters through transporters such as M C T eight. Inside the cell, D two often makes T three from T four. So the T three inside a cell need not match the T three in plasma. In mice lacking D two, body temperature fell in the cold, because brown fat made less heat. Yet plasma T three was normal. Keep the rule. The thyroid sends mostly T four, and the ring that loses its iodine decides: on or off.
